# Step 6 — gauged R² action through two physical fermions

## 1. Problem and Target

Construct the physical bosonic and quadratic-fermion terms of the already assembled primed BF invariant. The starting point is [Step 4 Eq. (47)](06_step4_Gold_unprimed_vector_and_gauge.md), with the complete primed map of [Step 5](08_step5_primed_composite_vector_insertion.md). Step 5a counted only explicitly written fermions; this step also expands the fermions inside hatted strengths, constrained vectors, conformal boxes, dependent connections, and the gauged Coomans–Özkan composites.

The aligned-triplet representation uses

```math
\sigma=1,\qquad b_\mu=0,\qquad\psi^i=0,\qquad
L^{ij}=L_{ij}=\frac{L}{\sqrt2}\delta^{ij},\qquad L>0.
\tag{1}
```

The defining gaugino $`\psi^i`$ vanishes, but the gravitino $`\psi_\mu^i`$ and original linear fermion $`\varphi^i`$ remain. The scalar $`L`$ is not set to a constant. No field equation, auxiliary elimination, vacuum condition, dualization, or expansion in $`g`$ is used.

The answer is an explicit finite component representation: every projected component is calculated below, and all 42 source groups are multiplied and separated into physical degree zero and two. The final action is the sum of those displayed products. This retains useful composite structure instead of printing thousands of repeated copies of the same scalar and spinor expressions. In particular, the projections are definitions of already existing fields, not extra independent fields or replacements for the calculation.

## 3. Definitions and Required Identities

### 3.1 Physical degree, independent fields, and the finite expansion

Introduce a commuting bookkeeping parameter $`t`$ only to define coefficients:

```math
\psi_\mu\mapsto t\psi_\mu,\qquad\varphi\mapsto t\varphi,
\qquad
[X]_n=\left.\frac1{n!}\frac{d^nX(t)}{dt^n}\right|_{t=0}.
\tag{2}
```

The independent bosons held fixed in this definition are $`e_\mu{}^a,C_\mu,B_{\mu\nu},E_{\mu\nu\rho},L,N,V_\mu{}^{ij}`$. Thus the supercovariant constrained component $`E_a`$ is not treated as a purely bosonic independent coordinate. For an even component $`X=X_{[0]}+t^2X_{[2]}+O(t^4)`$ and an odd component $`\zeta=t\zeta_{[1]}+O(t^3)`$. Brackets $`[X]_n`$ and superscripts $`X^{(n)}`$ in the background derivation below denote this same coefficient.

```math
\begin{aligned}
[XY]_0&=[X]_0[Y]_0,\\
[XY]_2&=[X]_2[Y]_0+[X]_0[Y]_2,\\
[XYZ]_2&=[X]_2[Y]_0[Z]_0+[X]_0[Y]_2[Z]_0+[X]_0[Y]_0[Z]_2,\\
[\bar\zeta\Gamma\eta]_2&=[\bar\zeta]_1\Gamma[\eta]_1,\\
[X^2]_2&=2[X]_0[X]_2\quad\text{for commuting scalar }X.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
```

No spinor is reordered in these rules. In particular no Grassmann sign occurs when choosing which even factor contributes degree two.

The ordinary forms and the constrained-vector completion are

```math
\begin{aligned}
G_{\mu\nu}&=2\partial_{[\mu}C_{\nu]},\\
H_{\mu\nu\rho}&=3\partial_{[\mu}B_{\nu\rho]}+\frac32C_{[\mu}G_{\nu\rho]}+\frac g2E_{\mu\nu\rho},\\
H^{ab}&=-\frac1{12}\varepsilon^{abcde}H_{cde},\\
[E^a]_0&=-\frac1{12}\varepsilon^{abcde}\nabla_bE_{cde},\\
[E^a]_2&=-\frac i2\bar\psi_b{}^i\gamma^{ba}\varphi_i
-\frac14\bar\psi_b{}^i\gamma^{abc}\psi_c{}^jL_{ij}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
```

Equation (4) follows by solving the source identity $`P^a=E^a+i\bar\psi_b\gamma^{ba}\varphi/2+\bar\psi_b^i\gamma^{abc}\psi_c^jL_{ij}/4`$, with $`P^a=-\varepsilon^{abcde}\nabla_bE_{cde}/12`$ (Özkan (3.12)–(3.13)). The ordinary three-form is held fixed, so the two displayed bilinears really belong to degree two.

### 3.2 Complete gauged background coefficients

This appendix owns only the background substitution. The gauge is $`\sigma=1`$, $`b_\mu=0`$, $`\psi^i=0`$, while $`\psi_\mu^i`$, $`\varphi^i`$, and the complete triplet $`L^{ij}`$ remain. This background calculation is valid before alignment; the main calculation subsequently applies Eq. (1). Projection labels $`(0),(1),(2)`$ count physical elementary fermions, including those inside dependent connections and hatted curvatures. They are not new fields.

Sources: Coomans–Özkan (2013), Eqs. (2.5)–(2.8), (5.2)–(5.7); Özkan (2016), Appendix A; the primary Bergshoeff et al. Weyl-multiplets paper, Eqs. (3.4), (3.6), (3.18), (3.20). The latter source is the 2001 Weyl-multiplets paper identified in the [bibliography](../../../../../../references/bibliography.md). The inherited project correction is $`\widehat R'(M)|_\chi=+8\bar\psi e\gamma\chi`$, not a claimed published erratum.

Conventions: five dimensions, mostly-plus metric, $`\varepsilon^{01234}=+1`$, unit-weight brackets, $`\gamma^{abcde}=i\varepsilon^{abcde}`$, gamma-dot without factorial, NW–SE lowering $`X_i=X^j\varepsilon_{ji}`$, $`\varepsilon_{12}=\varepsilon^{12}=1`$. Scalar $`i`$ is preserved by the operational transpose bar. Ordinary $`\nabla`$ on spinors contains the Levi–Civita spin connection and the unreduced $`SU(2)`$ connection. Lorentz curvature contractions use the inherited Coomans order.

#### Background: 1. Physical grading and independent bosonic strengths

Bosonic fields and their ordinary derivatives have degree zero; $`\psi_\mu^i`$, $`\varphi^i`$ and their ordinary covariant derivatives have degree one. The norm and its derivative are

```math
L^2=L^{ij}L_{ij},\qquad L>0,\qquad
\partial_\mu L=L^{-1}L_{ij}\nabla_\mu L^{ij}.
\tag{B1}
```

No inverse-power fermion expansion of $`L`$ is needed, because this norm is an independent bosonic triplet norm. When a supercovariant derivative acts on it, its degree-two correction must nevertheless be retained.

```math
G_{\mu\nu}=2\partial_{[\mu}C_{\nu]},\quad
H_{\mu\nu\rho}=3\partial_{[\mu}B_{\nu\rho]}+\frac32C_{[\mu}G_{\nu\rho]}+\frac g2E_{\mu\nu\rho},\quad
H^{ab}=-\frac1{12}\varepsilon^{abcde}H_{cde}.
\tag{B2}
```

From the source supercovariant strengths on the stated gauge,

```math
\widehat G_{ab}=G_{ab}+\frac i2\bar\psi_{[a}\psi_{b]},\qquad
\widehat H_{abc}=H_{abc}-\frac34\bar\psi_{[a}\gamma_b\psi_{c]}.
\tag{B3}
```

The original constrained $`E_a`$, if treated through its three-form, also has hidden fermions. Coomans (3.2)–(3.3) gives

```math
E^{a(0)}=-\frac1{12}\varepsilon^{abcde}\nabla_bE_{cde},\qquad
E^{a(2)}=-\frac i2\bar\psi_b\gamma^{ba}\varphi
-\frac14\bar\psi_b{}^i\gamma^{abc}\psi_c{}^jL_{ij}.
\tag{B4}
```

The original triplet, scalar $`N`$, and three-form remain unaligned independent inputs.

#### Background: 2. Tensor composite

Coomans (5.6) becomes

```math
T_{ab}=\frac18\widehat G_{ab}+\frac1{48}\varepsilon_{abcde}\widehat H^{cde}.
\tag{B5}
```

Insert (B3) term by term. The bosonic dual obeys $`\varepsilon_{abcde}H^{cde}=-12H_{ab}`$. Therefore

```math
T_{ab}^{(0)}=\frac18G_{ab}-\frac{12}{48}H_{ab}
=\frac18(G_{ab}-2H_{ab}),
\tag{B6}
```

```math
T_{ab}^{(2)}=\frac18\frac i2\bar\psi_{[a}\psi_{b]}
+\frac1{48}\left(-\frac34\right)\varepsilon_{abcde}\bar\psi^c\gamma^d\psi^e
=\frac i{16}\bar\psi_{[a}\psi_{b]}-\frac1{64}\varepsilon_{abcde}\bar\psi^c\gamma^d\psi^e.
\tag{B7}
```

#### Background: 3. Acyclic dependent S connection and Q curvature

The torsion correction has physical degree two:

```math
\omega_\mu{}^{ab}=\omega_\mu{}^{ab}(e)+K_\mu{}^{ab},\qquad
K_\mu{}^{ab}=\frac12\bar\psi^{[a}\gamma^{b]}\psi_\mu+\frac14\bar\psi^a\gamma_\mu\psi^b.
\tag{B8}
```

Here $`K`$ labels the difference of the existing dependent connection and its Levi–Civita part, not an independent field. Its contribution to a derivative of a single fermion is cubic and is omitted only in degree-one expressions. First construct the Q curvature with its S-connection term omitted:

```math
\widehat R'_{\mu\nu}{}^{i(1)}(Q)
=2\nabla_{[\mu}\psi_{\nu]}^i
+\frac i4\gamma^{cd}(G_{cd}-2H_{cd})\gamma_{[\mu}\psi_{\nu]}^i.
\tag{B9}
```

Then form the S connection, and only afterwards the complete Q curvature:

```math
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\mu^{i(1)}={}&\frac i3\gamma^a
\left[2\nabla_{[\mu}\psi_{a]}^i+\frac i4\gamma^{cd}(G_{cd}-2H_{cd})\gamma_{[\mu}\psi_{a]}^i\right]\\
&-\frac i{24}\gamma_\mu\gamma^{ab}
\left[2\nabla_{[a}\psi_{b]}^i+\frac i4\gamma^{cd}(G_{cd}-2H_{cd})\gamma_{[a}\psi_{b]}^i\right],
\end{aligned}
\tag{B10}
```

```math
\widehat R_{\mu\nu}^{i(1)}(Q)=\widehat R'_{\mu\nu}{}^{i(1)}(Q)-2i\gamma_{[\mu}\phi_{\nu]}^{i(1)},\qquad
\gamma^\mu\widehat R_{\mu\nu}^{i(1)}(Q)=0.
\tag{B11}
```

Thus (B9), then (B10), then (B11) is an acyclic substitution order. The prime on $`R'`$ means omission of the dependent S connection, not the primed vector multiplet.

#### Background: 4. The vanishing defining gaugino has a nonzero derivative

The source vector derivative must be restricted after its complete definition is written. Its $`Y^{ij}\psi_{\mu j}`$ term uses $`Y^{ij}=-gL^{ij}/2`$:

```math
\begin{aligned}
(\mathcal D_\mu\psi^i)^{(1)}
&=\left(\frac14\gamma^{ab}G_{ab}-\gamma^{ab}T_{ab}^{(0)}\right)\psi_\mu^i
-\frac g2L^{ij}\psi_{\mu j}-\phi_\mu^{i(1)}\\
&=\frac18\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}+2H_{ab})\psi_\mu^i
-\frac g2L^{ij}\psi_{\mu j}-\phi_\mu^{i(1)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B12}
```

```math
(\mathcal D_\mu\psi_i)^{(1)}
=\frac18\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}+2H_{ab})\psi_{\mu i}
+\frac g2L_{ij}\psi_\mu^j-\phi_{\mu i}^{(1)}.
\tag{B13}
```

The gauged spinor map (5.3) retains its differentiated-gaugino term even though each undifferentiated defining gaugino is zero:

```math
\chi^{i(1)}=\frac i8\gamma^\mu
\left[\frac18\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}+2H_{ab})\psi_\mu^i
-\frac g2L^{ij}\psi_{\mu j}-\phi_\mu^{i(1)}\right]
+\frac g8\varphi^i.
\tag{B14}
```

Lowering acts on this entire bracket: $`\chi_i^{(1)}=\chi^{r(1)}\varepsilon_{ri}`$. Equations (B10) and (B14) express all spinors in elementary fields without a cyclic dependence.

#### Background: 5. Lorentz-curvature source reconciliation and trace

Coomans (2.6) and Özkan Appendix A print a naked $`i\bar\psi_{[\mu}\gamma^{ab}\psi_{\nu]}`$ in addition to the S-connection term. The primary Weyl paper gives the undeformed Lorentz curvature with **only** $`i\bar\phi_{[\mu}\gamma^{ab}\psi_{\nu]}`$ in Eq. (3.4). Its Eq. (3.20) and the rule (3.6) determine the remaining supercovariant corrections. The second line of (3.20), containing $`T`$, changes the QQ structure function; only its last line belongs to the deformation $`M`$. Therefore one must not apply the $`-2\psi M`$ rule to the $`T`$ line a second time. This fixes coefficient $`i`$ for the tensor term. The naked gravitino term has the wrong Weyl weight and is omitted under this explicit primary-source reconciliation; it is not replaced by another S-connection term. This is a source-reconciled project input, not an asserted published erratum.

The f-independent Lorentz curvature needed here, through degree two, is consequently

```math
\begin{aligned}
\widehat R'_{\mu\nu}{}^{ab}(M)={}&R_{\mu\nu}{}^{ab}(\omega)
+i\bar\phi_{[\mu}^{(1)}\gamma^{ab}\psi_{\nu]}
+i\bar\psi_{[\mu}\gamma^{[a}\gamma\!\cdot T^{(0)}\gamma^{b]}\psi_{\nu]}\\
&+\bar\psi_{[\mu}\gamma^{[a}\widehat R_{\nu]}{}^{b](1)}(Q)
+\frac12\bar\psi_{[\mu}\gamma_{\nu]}\widehat R^{ab(1)}(Q)
+8\bar\psi_{[\mu}e_{\nu]}{}^{[a}\gamma^{b]}\chi^{(1)}+O(\mathrm{fermion}^4).
\end{aligned}
\tag{B15}
```

The sign of the last term is the inherited project correction. The Ricci contraction and trace use

```math
f_\mu{}^a=-\frac16\mathcal R_\mu{}^a+\frac1{48}e_\mu{}^a\mathcal R,
\qquad f_a{}^a=\left(-\frac16+\frac5{48}\right)\mathcal R=-\frac1{16}\mathcal R.
\tag{B16}
```

Here $`\mathcal R`$ denotes only the double trace of (B15). It is not the Levi–Civita scalar at nonzero fermion degree. The two Q-curvature terms have zero trace: their contractions reduce to $`\gamma^a\widehat R_{ab}(Q)`$ or the antisymmetric trace $`\widehat R_a{}^a(Q)`$, both zero by (B11) and antisymmetry. Explicitly the first such trace is

```math
\frac14\left[
\bar\psi_a\gamma^a\widehat R_b{}^b
-\bar\psi_a\gamma^b\widehat R_b{}^a
-\bar\psi_b\gamma^a\widehat R_a{}^b
+\bar\psi_b\gamma^b\widehat R_a{}^a
\right]=0,
\qquad
\frac12\bar\psi_{[a}\gamma_{b]}\widehat R^{ab}=0.
\tag{B17}
```

The chi trace is

```math
8\bar\psi_{[a}\delta_{b]}{}^{[a}\gamma^{b]}\chi
=\frac84(1-5-5+1)\bar\psi_a\gamma^a\chi
=-16\bar\psi_a\gamma^a\chi.
\tag{B18}
```

The spin-connection curvature through degree two has no $`K^2`$ term:

```math
\bigl(R(\omega)-R(\omega(e))\bigr)^{(2)}
=2e^\mu{}_ae^\nu{}_b\nabla^{\rm LC}_{[\mu}K_{\nu]}{}^{ab}.
\tag{B19}
```

Combining (B15)–(B19) gives

```math
(f_a{}^a)^{(0)}=-\frac1{16}R(\omega(e)),
\tag{B20}
```

```math
\begin{aligned}
(f_a{}^a)^{(2)}={}&-\frac18e^\mu{}_ae^\nu{}_b\nabla^{\rm LC}_{[\mu}K_{\nu]}{}^{ab}
-\frac i{16}\bar\phi_a^{(1)}\gamma^{ab}\psi_b\\
&-\frac i{128}\bar\psi_a\gamma^{[a}\gamma^{cd}(G_{cd}-2H_{cd})\gamma^{b]}\psi_b
+\bar\psi_a\gamma^a\chi^{(1)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B21}
```

Every term on the right is fixed by (B8), (B10), and (B14).

#### Background: 6. Scalar D: distributed coefficients

The constant compensator has a nonzero conformal box:

```math
(\Box_c\sigma)^{(0+2)}=2f_a{}^a
-\frac i2\bar\psi_a{}^i(\mathcal D^a\psi^r)^{(1)}\varepsilon_{ri}
-2\bar\psi_a{}^i\gamma^a\chi_i^{(1)}.
\tag{B22}
```

The source ordinary $`G^2`$ term and its explicit gravitino bilinear combine to $`-\widehat G^2/16`$ at the retained order. With (5.2), (5.4), this gives

```math
D=\frac12f_a{}^a-\frac1{16}\widehat G^2-\frac{26}{3}T^2+2\widehat G^{ab}T_{ab}
+\frac g4N+\frac{g^2}{16}L^2
-\frac i8\bar\psi_a{}^i(\mathcal D^a\psi^r)^{(1)}\varepsilon_{ri}
-\frac12\bar\psi_a{}^i\gamma^a\chi_i^{(1)}+O(\mathrm{fermion}^4).
\tag{B23}
```

At degree zero the coefficient arithmetic is

```math
\begin{aligned}
-\frac1{16}G^2-\frac{13}{96}(G-2H)^2+\frac14G(G-2H)
&=\frac{-6-13+24}{96}G^2+\frac{52-48}{96}GH-\frac{52}{96}H^2\\
&=\frac5{96}G^2+\frac1{24}GH-\frac{13}{24}H^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B24}
```

```math
D^{(0)}=-\frac1{32}R(\omega(e))+\frac5{96}G^2+\frac1{24}GH-\frac{13}{24}H^2+\frac g4N+\frac{g^2}{16}L^2.
\tag{B25}
```

For degree two the tensor terms distribute as follows:

```math
\begin{aligned}
&-\frac18G\widehat G^{(2)}-\frac{52}{3}T^{(0)}T^{(2)}+2GT^{(2)}+2\widehat G^{(2)}T^{(0)}\\
&=\left(\frac18G-\frac12H\right)\widehat G^{(2)}
+\left(-\frac16G+\frac{13}{3}H\right)T^{(2)}\\
&=\left(\frac i{16}G-\frac i4H-\frac i{96}G+\frac{13i}{48}H\right)^{ab}\bar\psi_a\psi_b
+\left(\frac1{384}G-\frac{13}{192}H\right)^{ab}\varepsilon_{abcde}\bar\psi^c\gamma^d\psi^e\\
&=\left(\frac{5i}{96}G^{ab}+\frac i{48}H^{ab}\right)\bar\psi_a\psi_b
+\left(\frac1{384}G^{ab}-\frac{13}{192}H^{ab}\right)\varepsilon_{abcde}\bar\psi^c\gamma^d\psi^e.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B26}
```

Hence the full degree-two result is

```math
\begin{aligned}
D^{(2)}={}&\frac12(f_a{}^a)^{(2)}
+\left(\frac{5i}{96}G^{ab}+\frac i{48}H^{ab}\right)\bar\psi_a\psi_b
+\left(\frac1{384}G^{ab}-\frac{13}{192}H^{ab}\right)\varepsilon_{abcde}\bar\psi^c\gamma^d\psi^e\\
&-\frac i8\bar\psi_a{}^i(\mathcal D^a\psi^r)^{(1)}\varepsilon_{ri}
-\frac12\bar\psi_a{}^i\gamma^a\chi_i^{(1)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{B27}
```

#### Background: 7. Required curvature and tensor-derivative completions

Coomans (2.6) gives the unaligned SU(2) curvature projections

```math
\widehat R_{\mu\nu}^{ij(0)}(V)=2\partial_{[\mu}V_{\nu]}^{ij}-2V_{[\mu}^{k(i}V_{\nu]k}{}^{j)},
\tag{B28}
```

```math
\begin{aligned}
\widehat R_{\mu\nu}^{ij(2)}(V)
={}&-\frac{3i}{2}\left(\bar\phi_{[\mu}^{i(1)}\psi_{\nu]}^j+\bar\phi_{[\mu}^{j(1)}\psi_{\nu]}^i\right)\\
&-4\left(\bar\psi_{[\mu}^i\gamma_{\nu]}\chi^{j(1)}+\bar\psi_{[\mu}^j\gamma_{\nu]}\chi^{i(1)}\right)\\
&-\frac i{16}\left(\bar\psi_{[\mu}^i\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}-2H_{ab})\psi_{\nu]}^j+\bar\psi_{[\mu}^j\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}-2H_{ab})\psi_{\nu]}^i\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{B29}
```

The SU(2) symmetrizations have been distributed explicitly in (B29).

The tensor jet is fixed by Coomans (2.5). At $`b_\mu=0`$ its zero and two projections are

```math
(\mathcal D_\mu T_{ab})^{(0)}=\nabla_\mu T_{ab}^{(0)},
\tag{B30}
```

```math
(\mathcal D_\mu T_{ab})^{(2)}
=\nabla_\mu T_{ab}^{(2)}-2K_\mu{}^c{}_{[a}T_{b]c}^{(0)}
-\frac i2\bar\psi_\mu\gamma_{ab}\chi^{(1)}
+\frac{3i}{32}\bar\psi_\mu\widehat R_{ab}^{(1)}(Q).
\tag{B31}
```

The derivative on (B7) is an ordinary covariant product derivative and acts on both gravitini. Likewise the first term of (B31) is not a replacement for the last three terms.

The source maps were read directly; Coomans p. 6 was inspected visually in memory. The D coefficients were distributed in (B24), (B26); the Q-curvature and chi traces are displayed in (B17), (B18). All retained expressions have their declared physical degree. The zero-fermion result matches the background used in the preceding Gold bosonic comparison. ### 3.3 Alignment retains connection and fermion terms

For the lower triplet, define the ordinary source derivative explicitly:

```math
\nabla_a L_{ij}=\partial_a L_{ij}+2V_{a(i}{}^kL_{j)k},\qquad
\nabla_a\varphi_i=(\partial_a+\tfrac14\omega^{\rm LC}_a{}^{bc}\gamma_{bc})\varphi_i-V_{a i}{}^j\varphi_j.
\tag{5}
```

In ordinary matrix notation, the aligned triplet gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\nabla_aL^{ij}]&=\frac{\partial_aL}{\sqrt2}\mathbf1+
\frac L{\sqrt2}([V_a]\varepsilon-\varepsilon[V_a]),\\
[\nabla_aL_{ij}]&=\frac{\partial_aL}{\sqrt2}\mathbf1+
\frac L{\sqrt2}(\varepsilon[V_a]-[V_a]\varepsilon),\\
[\mathcal D_aL_{ij}]_2&=-i\bar\psi_{a(i}\varphi_{j)},\\
[\mathcal D_aL]_2&=-iL^{-1}L^{ij}\bar\psi_{a(i}\varphi_{j)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
```

Thus neither $`\nabla_aL_{ij}`$ nor $`\mathcal D_aL_{ij}`$ is set to zero. Raising both triplet indices always uses two epsilon tensors, including for the degree-two term in (6).

## 4. Detailed Derivation

### 4.1 Expand the original linear-fermion derivative

The degree-one part of the source lower-index derivative (Step 5 Eq. (22), itself fixed against Coomans (2.21)) is

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\mathcal D_a\varphi_i]_1={}&\nabla_a\varphi_i
-\frac i2\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})\psi_a{}^j
+\frac i2\gamma^b[E_b]_0\psi_{ai}-\frac12N\psi_{ai}\\
&-\frac18L_{ij}\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\psi_a{}^j
+3L_{ij}[\phi_a{}^j]_1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
```

Terms $`K\varphi`$, $`[\mathcal D L]_2\psi`$, $`[E]_2\psi`$, and $`[T]_2\psi`$ have three fermions and are discarded here. They first contribute to the even action at degree four. This is the actual reason they may be omitted.

### 4.2 Scalar and spinor of the primed vector

The scalar map gives directly

```math
[\rho']_0=\frac{2N}{L},\qquad
[\rho']_2=iL^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j,
\tag{8}
```

and multiplication gives

```math
[(\rho')^2]_0=\frac{4N^2}{L^2},\qquad
[(\rho')^2]_2=\frac{4iN}{L^4}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j.
\tag{9}
```

The full linear-in-fermions gaugino follows by dropping only the cubic terms of Step 5 Eq. (4):

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\lambda'_i]_1={}&-2iL^{-1}\gamma^a[\mathcal D_a\varphi_i]_1
+16L^{-1}L_{ij}[\chi^j]_1
+\frac1{2L}\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}-2H_{ab})\varphi_i\\
&-2NL^{-3}L_{ij}\varphi^j
+2iL^{-3}\gamma^a(\nabla_aL_{ij})L^{jk}\varphi_k
-2iL^{-3}\gamma^a[E_a]_0L_{ij}\varphi^j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
```

For clarity, insert (7) and the background $`\chi_1`$ into the first two terms separately:

```math
\begin{aligned}
-2iL^{-1}\gamma^a[\mathcal D_a\varphi_i]_1={}&
-2iL^{-1}\gamma^a\nabla_a\varphi_i
-L^{-1}\gamma^a\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})\psi_a{}^j\\
&+L^{-1}\gamma^a\gamma^b[E_b]_0\psi_{ai}
+iNL^{-1}\gamma^a\psi_{ai}\\
&+\frac{i}{4L}L_{ij}\gamma^a\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\psi_a{}^j
-\frac{6i}{L}L_{ij}\gamma^a[\phi_a{}^j]_1,\\
16L^{-1}L_{ij}[\chi^j]_1={}&
\frac{i}{4L}L_{ij}\gamma^a\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}+2H_{bc})\psi_a{}^j\\
&-\frac{ig}{L}L_{ij}L^{jk}\gamma^a\psi_{ak}
-\frac{2i}{L}L_{ij}\gamma^a[\phi_a{}^j]_1
+\frac{2g}{L}L_{ij}\varphi^j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
```

The scalar coefficients in the first line come from $`(-2i)(-i/2)=-1`$, $`(-2i)(i/2)=1`$, and $`(-2i)(-1/2)=i`$. The two $`H`$-dependent gravitino terms in (11) cancel; the two $`G`$ terms add. The exact two-dimensional identity $`L_{ij}L^{jk}=L^2\delta_i{}^k/2`$ reduces the gauging term. Finally the explicit S-connection projector gives

```math
\gamma^a[\phi_a{}^i]_1
=i\left(\frac13-\frac5{24}\right)\gamma^{ab}[R'_{ab}{}^i(Q)]_1
=\frac i8\gamma^{ab}[R'_{ab}{}^i(Q)]_1.
\tag{12}
```

Thus the completely substituted gaugino is

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\lambda'_i]_1={}&-\frac{2i}{L}\gamma^a\nabla_a\varphi_i
+\frac1{2L}\gamma^{ab}(G_{ab}-2H_{ab})\varphi_i
+\left(\frac{2g}{L}-\frac{2N}{L^3}\right)L_{ij}\varphi^j\\
&+\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^a(\nabla_aL_{ij})L^{jk}\varphi_k
-\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^a[E_a]_0L_{ij}\varphi^j\\
&-\frac1L\gamma^a\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})\psi_a{}^j
+\frac1L\gamma^a\gamma^b[E_b]_0\psi_{ai}
+i\left(\frac NL-\frac{gL}{2}\right)\gamma^a\psi_{ai}\\
&+\frac{i}{2L}L_{ij}\gamma^a\gamma^{bc}G_{bc}\psi_a{}^j
+\frac2L L_{ij}\gamma^{ab}\nabla_a\psi_b{}^j\\
&+\frac{i}{4L}L_{ij}\gamma^{ab}\gamma^{cd}(G_{cd}-2H_{cd})\gamma_a\psi_b{}^j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
```

No gauge condition on the gravitino is used in (12) or (13). All $`L_{ij}`$ in this result are the aligned triplet from (1), whose derivatives are (6).

The barred gaugino is fixed term by term without an independent ansatz. For any one summand $`cM\zeta_i`$ of (13),

```math
\overline{cM\zeta_i}=c\bar\zeta_i\,C^{-1}M^TC,
\qquad
[\bar\lambda'{}^i]_1=\varepsilon^{ir}\overline{[\lambda'_r]_1}.
\tag{14}
```

For the gamma strings that occur in (13), the exact replacement table is

```math
\begin{array}{c|c}
M&C^{-1}M^TC\\\hline
1&1\\
\gamma^a&\gamma^a\\
\gamma^{ab}&-\gamma^{ab}\\
\gamma^a\gamma^b&\gamma^b\gamma^a\\
\gamma^a\gamma^{bc}&-\gamma^{bc}\gamma^a\\
\gamma^{ab}\gamma^{cd}\gamma_a&\gamma_a\gamma^{cd}\gamma^{ab}
\end{array}
\tag{15}
```

Equations (13)–(15) specify every bar with no Grassmann interchange. For example $`\overline{-2i\gamma^a\nabla_a\varphi_i/L}=-2i(\nabla_a\bar\varphi_i)\gamma^a/L`$ and the third gamma-string row in (15) supplies the minus sign for the flux bilinear.

### 4.3 Triplet through physical degree two

The conformal box is expanded before inserting it into $`Y'`$. Its upper-index coefficients are

```math
[\Box_cL^{ij}]_0=\nabla^a\nabla_aL^{ij}+6[f_a{}^a]_0L^{ij},
\tag{16}
```

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\Box_cL^{ij}]_2={}&\nabla^a[\mathcal D_aL^{ij}]_2
+K_b{}^{ba}\nabla_aL^{ij}+6[f_a{}^a]_2L^{ij}
-i\bar\psi^{a(i}[\mathcal D_a\varphi^{j)}]_1\\
&+4\bar\psi^{a(i}\gamma_a[\chi^{k)}]_1L^j{}_k
+4\bar\psi^{a(j}\gamma_a[\chi^{k)}]_1L^i{}_k
-6L^{ij}\bar\psi_a\gamma^a[\chi]_1\\
&-\bar\varphi^{(i}\gamma^{bc}[T_{bc}]_0\gamma^a\psi_a{}^{j)}
+\bar\varphi^{(i}\gamma^a[\phi_a{}^{j)}]_1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
```

This is the degree-two expansion of Özkan (3.15); lower both free indices with epsilon to obtain $`[\Box_cL_{ij}]_n`$. The first term is explicitly $`-i\nabla^a(\bar\psi_a{}^{(i}\varphi^{j)})`$, whose derivative is $`-i(\nabla^a\bar\psi_a{}^{(i})\varphi^{j)}-i\bar\psi_a{}^{(i}\nabla^a\varphi^{j)}`$. The separate $`-i\bar\psi[\mathcal D\varphi]_1`$ term in (17) must also remain.

The degree-zero triplet is

```math
\begin{aligned}
[Y'_{ij}]_0={}&L^{-1}[\Box_cL_{ij}]_0
-L^{-3}L^{km}(\nabla_aL_{k(i})(\nabla^aL_{j)m})
-L^{-3}L_{ij}(N^2+[E_a]_0[E^a]_0)\\
&+2L^{-3}[E_a]_0L_{k(i}\nabla^aL_{j)}{}^k
+\frac83L^{-1}L_{ij}[T_{ab}]_0[T^{ab}]_0
+4L^{-1}L_{ij}[D]_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
```

Applying (3) separately to all seven even terms gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
[Y'_{ij}]_2={}&L^{-1}[\Box_cL_{ij}]_2\\
&-L^{-3}L^{km}\bigl(
[\mathcal D_aL_{k(i}]_2\nabla^aL_{j)m}
+\nabla_aL_{k(i}[\mathcal D^aL_{j)m}]_2\bigr)\\
&-2L^{-3}L_{ij}[E_a]_0[E^a]_2\\
&+2L^{-3}[E_a]_2L_{k(i}\nabla^aL_{j)}{}^k
+2L^{-3}[E_a]_0L_{k(i}[\mathcal D^aL_{j)}{}^k]_2\\
&+\frac{16}{3}L^{-1}L_{ij}[T_{ab}]_0[T^{ab}]_2
+4L^{-1}L_{ij}[D]_2\\
&+iNL^{-3}\bar\varphi_{(i}\varphi_{j)}
-3iNL^{-5}L_{ij}L^{kl}\bar\varphi_k\varphi_l\\
&+3L^{-5}L_{ij}L^{kl}\bar\varphi_k\gamma^a[E_a]_0\varphi_l
-L^{-3}\bar\varphi_{(i}\gamma^a[E_a]_0\varphi_{j)}\\
&-16iL^{-1}[\bar\chi_{(i}]_1\varphi_{j)}
+16iL^{-3}L_{ij}L_{kl}[\bar\chi^k]_1\varphi^l\\
&+2L^{-3}L_{k(i}\bar\varphi^k\gamma^a[\mathcal D_a\varphi_{j)}]_1
-3L^{-5}L_{k(i}L^{lm}\bar\varphi^k\gamma^a(\nabla_aL_{j)l})\varphi_m\\
&+\frac12L^{-3}\bar\varphi^l\gamma^a(\nabla_aL_{l(i})\varphi_{j)}
+\frac12L^{-3}\bar\varphi^m\gamma^a(\nabla_aL_{ij})\varphi_m
+2iL^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi\gamma^{ab}[T_{ab}]_0\varphi.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
```

All slots on the right are already explicit in (4), (6), (7), (16), (17), and the background derivation. The three explicit quartic terms in the parent triplet have degree four and are omitted. The two $`E`$ cross terms and the $`T_0T_2`$ term in (19) are absent in a merely explicit-spinor count; they are retained here.

### 4.4 Ordinary potential, ordinary strength, and hatted strength

Use the already derived local Gold-(25) potential from Step 5, now separating the constrained-vector completion in (4):

```math
\begin{aligned}
[A'_\mu]_0&=2L^{-1}[E_\mu]_0+\sqrt2V_\mu,\\
[A'_\mu]_2&=2L^{-1}[E_\mu]_2
-L^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\gamma_\mu\varphi^j
-iL^{-1}\bar\varphi^i\psi_{\mu i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
```

The trace connection is defined by $`V_\mu{}^{ij}=V'_\mu{}^{ij}+\delta^{ij}V_\mu/2`$, $`\delta_{ij}V'_\mu{}^{ij}=0`$. This connection prime is not a new vector-multiplet label.

The ordinary curl gives

```math
[F'_{ab}]_0=4\nabla_{[a}(L^{-1}[E_{b]}]_0)+2\sqrt2\partial_{[a}V_{b]},
\tag{21}
```

where the last term means $`2\sqrt2e_a{}^\mu e_b{}^\nu\partial_{[\mu}V_{\nu]}`$, not a nonholonomic partial derivative of frame components. All other curls of frame one-forms below are likewise world curls converted to the frame, or equivalently Levi–Civita antisymmetric covariant derivatives.

Distributing the derivative over all four products in (20) gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
[F'_{ab}]_2={}&4L^{-1}\nabla_{[a}[E_{b]}]_2
-4L^{-2}(\partial_{[a}L)[E_{b]}]_2\\
&+6L^{-4}(\partial_{[a}L)L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\gamma_{b]}\varphi^j
-2L^{-3}(\nabla_{[a}L_{ij})\bar\varphi^i\gamma_{b]}\varphi^j\\
&-2L^{-3}L_{ij}(\nabla_{[a}\bar\varphi^i)\gamma_{b]}\varphi^j
-2L^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\gamma_{[b}\nabla_{a]}\varphi^j\\
&+2iL^{-2}(\partial_{[a}L)\bar\varphi^i\psi_{b]i}
-2iL^{-1}(\nabla_{[a}\bar\varphi^i)\psi_{b]i}
-2iL^{-1}\bar\varphi^i\nabla_{[a}\psi_{b]i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
```

All spinor derivatives in this ordinary curl are bosonic $`\nabla`$, not $`\mathcal D`$. The derivative of $`[E]_2`$ is fixed by the two explicit bilinears in (4) and the ordinary Leibniz rule. For example its first term is $`-i(\nabla\bar\psi_b)\gamma^{ba}\varphi/2-i\bar\psi_b\gamma^{ba}\nabla\varphi/2`$; its second gives three terms, with the derivative on each gravitino and on $`L_{ij}`$, all with coefficient $`-1/4`$.

The definition of the supercovariant vector strength, rather than a second potential ansatz, then gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\widehat F'_{ab}]_0&=[F'_{ab}]_0,\\
[\widehat F'_{ab}]_2&=[F'_{ab}]_2
-\bar\psi_{[a}{}^i\gamma_{b]}[\lambda'_i]_1
+\frac i2[\rho']_0\bar\psi_{[a}{}^i\psi_{b]i},\\
[\widehat G_{ab}]_0&=G_{ab},\\
[\widehat G_{ab}]_2&=\frac i2\bar\psi_{[a}{}^i\psi_{b]i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
```

The ordinary/hatted distinction is mandatory even at two fermions.

### 4.5 Derivative slots in the action

The scalar derivative and the gaugino derivative needed in the source density are

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\mathcal D_a\rho']_0&=2L^{-1}\partial_aN-2NL^{-2}\partial_aL,\\
[\mathcal D_a\rho']_2&=-3iL^{-4}(\partial_aL)L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j
+iL^{-3}(\nabla_aL_{ij})\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j\\
&\quad+iL^{-3}L_{ij}(\nabla_a\bar\varphi^i)\varphi^j
+iL^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\nabla_a\varphi^j
-\frac i2\bar\psi_a{}^i[\lambda'_i]_1,\\
[\mathcal D_a\lambda'_i]_1&=\nabla_a[\lambda'_i]_1
+\frac14\gamma^{bc}[F'_{bc}]_0\psi_{ai}
+\frac i2\gamma^b[\mathcal D_b\rho']_0\psi_{ai}\\
&\quad-[Y'_{ij}]_0\psi_a{}^j
-\frac{N}{4L}\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\psi_{ai}
-\frac{2N}{L}[\phi_{ai}]_1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
```

The slash in the projected action means $`[\not{\mathcal D}\lambda'_i]_1=\gamma^a[\mathcal D_a\lambda'_i]_1`$. The ordinary derivative of (13) is distributive. For any displayed summand $`c(L,N)\,M(L_{ij},G,H,E_0,\nabla L)\zeta`$ its actual differentiated expression is

```math
\nabla_a(cM\zeta)
=(\partial_Lc)(\partial_aL)M\zeta+(\partial_Nc)(\partial_aN)M\zeta
+c(\nabla_aM)\zeta+cM\nabla_a\zeta.
\tag{25}
```

In (25), apply $`\nabla`$ to each displayed factor of $`M`$ in its original order; $`\nabla\gamma=0`$. For instance the flux coefficient and the derivative-triplet coefficient give respectively

```math
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_a\left[\frac1{2L}\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\varphi_i\right]
={}&-\frac{\partial_aL}{2L^2}\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\varphi_i\\
&+\frac1{2L}\gamma^{bc}(\nabla_aG_{bc}-2\nabla_aH_{bc})\varphi_i
+\frac1{2L}\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})\nabla_a\varphi_i,\\
\nabla_a\left[\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})L^{jk}\varphi_k\right]
={}&-\frac{6i\partial_aL}{L^4}\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})L^{jk}\varphi_k\\
&+\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^b(\nabla_a\nabla_bL_{ij})L^{jk}\varphi_k
+\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})(\nabla_aL^{jk})\varphi_k\\
&+\frac{2i}{L^3}\gamma^b(\nabla_bL_{ij})L^{jk}\nabla_a\varphi_k.
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
```

No derivative ordering is changed. In particular no curvature commutator is needed or omitted.

The scalar box requires both the scalar derivative completion and the K connection:

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\Box_c\rho']_0&=\nabla^2\left(\frac{2N}{L}\right)+2[f_a{}^a]_0\frac{2N}{L},\\
[\Box_c\rho']_2&=\nabla^a[\mathcal D_a\rho']_2+K_b{}^{ba}\partial_a\left(\frac{2N}{L}\right)
-\frac i2\bar\psi_a{}^i[\mathcal D^a\lambda'_i]_1\\
&\quad-\frac{4N}{L}\bar\psi_a{}^i\gamma^a[\chi_i]_1
+\frac1{16}\bar\psi_a{}^i\gamma^a\gamma^{bc}(G_{bc}-2H_{bc})[\lambda'_i]_1\\
&\quad+\frac12[\bar\phi_a{}^i]_1\gamma^a[\lambda'_i]_1
+2[f_a{}^a]_0[\rho']_2+\frac{4N}{L}[f_a{}^a]_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{27}
```

The derivative on the four explicitly differentiated scalar bilinears in (24) acts by the same even Leibniz rule. The second derivative on a scalar quotient is, without integration by parts,

```math
\nabla^2\left(\frac{2N}{L}\right)
=\frac2L\nabla^2N-\frac{2N}{L^2}\nabla^2L
-\frac4{L^2}\partial_aL\partial^aN+\frac{4N}{L^3}(\partial L)^2.
\tag{28}
```

For the differentiated hatted strengths we must also remove the Q and S transformations, not merely differentiate their explicit bilinears. From Coomans (2.18), first convert the world-index variation to tangent indices. The inverse-vielbein variation adds $`-\bar\epsilon\gamma^c\psi_{[a}\widehat F_{|c|b]}`$. Replacing the parameters by the corresponding gauge fields and subtracting the transformation gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal D_c\widehat F_{ab}={}&\nabla^{\omega}_c\widehat F_{ab}
+\frac i2\rho\bar\psi_c\widehat R_{ab}(Q)
+\bar\psi_c\gamma_{[a}\mathcal D_{b]}\lambda\\
&-i\bar\psi_c\gamma_{[a}\gamma\!\cdot\!T\gamma_{b]}\lambda
-i\bar\phi_c\gamma_{ab}\lambda
+\bar\psi_c\gamma^d\psi_{[a}\widehat F_{|d|b]}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{29}
```

This equation is used once with the primed vector and once with the defining vector. Their explicit coefficient equations are

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\mathcal D_c\widehat F'_{ab}]_0={}&\nabla_c[F'_{ab}]_0,\\
[\mathcal D_c\widehat F'_{ab}]_2={}&\nabla_c[\widehat F'_{ab}]_2
-2K_c{}^d{}_{[a}[F'_{b]d}]_0
+\frac{iN}{L}\bar\psi_c{}^i[\widehat R_{ab i}(Q)]_1\\
&+\bar\psi_c{}^i\gamma_{[a}[\mathcal D_{b]}\lambda'_i]_1
-\frac i8\bar\psi_c{}^i\gamma_{[a}\gamma^{de}(G_{de}-2H_{de})\gamma_{b]}[\lambda'_i]_1\\
&-i[\bar\phi_c{}^i]_1\gamma_{ab}[\lambda'_i]_1
+\bar\psi_c{}^i\gamma^d\psi_{[a i}[F'_{|d|b]}]_0,\\
[\mathcal D_c\widehat G_{ab}]_0={}&\nabla_cG_{ab},\\
[\mathcal D_c\widehat G_{ab}]_2={}&\frac i2\nabla_c(\bar\psi_{[a}{}^i\psi_{b]i})-2K_c{}^d{}_{[a}G_{b]d}
+\frac i2\bar\psi_c{}^i[\widehat R_{ab i}(Q)]_1\\
&+\bar\psi_c{}^i\gamma_{[a}[\mathcal D_{b]}\psi_i]_1
+\bar\psi_c{}^i\gamma^d\psi_{[a i}G_{|d|b]}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
```

The $`\mathcal D\psi_i`$ in (30) is the nonzero defining-gaugino derivative from the background calculation. Terms explicitly proportional to the defining $`\lambda=\psi^i=0`$ vanish, whereas this derivative term survives.

The tensor derivative is independently fixed by Coomans (2.5):

```math
\begin{aligned}
[\mathcal D_cT_{ab}]_0&=\frac18\nabla_c(G_{ab}-2H_{ab}),\\
[\mathcal D_cT_{ab}]_2&=\nabla_c[T_{ab}]_2
-\frac14K_c{}^d{}_{[a}(G_{b]d}-2H_{b]d})
-\frac i2\bar\psi_c\gamma_{ab}[\chi]_1
+\frac{3i}{32}\bar\psi_c[\widehat R_{ab}(Q)]_1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
```

The divergences in the density are obtained by raising with the fixed frame metric and setting $`c=b`$; this operation introduces no fermion degree. Equations (29)–(31) make all differentiated background completions explicit.

For the remaining scalar contractions the substitution rules are

```math
\begin{aligned}
[T^2]_0&=\frac1{64}(G_{ab}-2H_{ab})(G^{ab}-2H^{ab}),\\
[T^2]_2&=\frac14(G^{ab}-2H^{ab})[T_{ab}]_2,\\
[\gamma\cdot T]_n&=\gamma^{ab}[T_{ab}]_n,\\
[\gamma\cdot\widehat G]_n&=\gamma^{ab}[\widehat G_{ab}]_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{32}
```

The ordinary derivative pieces in (17), (22), (27), (30), and (31) are products of original fields. The source-supercovariant operators have all been replaced by the finite equations above. Ordinary covariant derivatives are retained to keep Lorentz and $`SU(2)`$ covariance visible; their product expansion does not introduce hidden fermions.

## 5. Consistency Checks

### 5.1 Source ledger and physical order

The accepted 42 source groups contain 57 distributed source rows. The projection above contains **15 degree-zero rows and 80 degree-two rows**, before combining equal contractions or inserting repeated component expressions. Unlike Step 5a, a retained even composite contributes both its physical coefficients, and every odd composite contributes its explicitly calculated coefficient of degree one.

For example the first source group expands as

```math
\begin{aligned}
Y'^{ij}(t)Y'_{ij}(t)
={}&[Y'^{ij}]_0[Y'_{ij}]_0\\
&+t^2\bigl([Y'^{ij}]_2[Y'_{ij}]_0+[Y'^{ij}]_0[Y'_{ij}]_2\bigr)+O(t^4)\\
={}&[Y'^{ij}]_0[Y'_{ij}]_0+2t^2[Y'^{ij}]_0[Y'_{ij}]_2+O(t^4).
\end{aligned}
\tag{C1}
```

The last equality follows from commutativity of the two even triplets and relabeling the contracted indices. The source-row ledger retains the two contributions separately so neither insertion is lost. The kinetic bilinear is

```math
-\frac12\bar\lambda'{}^i(t)\not{\mathcal D}\lambda'_i(t)
=-\frac{t^2}{2}[\bar\lambda'{}^i]_1\gamma^a[\mathcal D_a\lambda'_i]_1+O(t^4).
\tag{C2}
```

The degree-three gaugino cannot contribute to (C2) at degree two. By contrast the tensor square contributes

```math
\begin{aligned}
[(\rho')^2T^2]_2
&=2[\rho']_0[\rho']_2[T_{ab}]_0[T^{ab}]_0
+2[\rho']_0^2[T_{ab}]_0[T^{ab}]_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C3}
```

The last term is a physical gravitino bilinear even though the original parent expression contained no explicit spinor.

The verifier independently expands the original source polynomial in a commuting degree parameter with noncommuting ordered atom labels, extracts coefficients zero and two, and compares them with the printed ledger. This tests all 57 source rows, their coefficients, and factor order. It does not substitute commuting numerical spinors for fermion bilinears.

### 5.2 Bosonic reduction and normalization

Set all elementary fermions to zero. Then every degree-two coefficient vanishes, as do $`\chi_1`$, $`\phi_1`$, $`K`$, and the nonzero-gaugino-derivative completion. The remaining potential-dependent terms can be integrated by parts using

```math
A'_a\nabla_bX^{ab}=\nabla_b(A'_aX^{ab})+\frac12F'_{ab}X^{ab},
\qquad
2\frac NL\nabla^2\frac NL=-2\left(\partial\frac NL\right)^2+
2\nabla_a\left(\frac NL\partial^a\frac NL\right).
\tag{C4}
```

The Chern–Simons conversion is the differential-form identity

```math
d(A'\wedge C\wedge F')=C\wedge F'\wedge F'-A'\wedge F'\wedge G.
\tag{C5}
```

These conversions are used only for this comparison; no boundary term has been discarded in the projected master density above. They are action equalities for compactly supported variations or boundary conditions that remove their surface integrals.

In the bosonic background,

```math
\begin{aligned}
8f_0-16D_0-\frac{416}{3}T_0^2+16GT_0
&=G^2-16GT_0-g^2L^2-4gN\\
&=-G^2+4GH-g^2L^2-4gN,\\
-\frac NL F'_0G+16\frac NL F'_0T_0
&=\frac NL GF'_0-4\frac NL HF'_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C6}
```

Subscripts zero in this comparison are the already defined physical projections. To compare the triplet with Gold's existing bold notation, raising (18) gives

```math
[Y'^{ij}]_0=\mathbf Y^{ij}+\left(\frac{gN}{L}+\frac{g^2L}{4}\right)L^{ij},
\tag{C7}
```

where explicitly

```math
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf Y^{ij}={}&L^{-1}\nabla^2L^{ij}
+L^{-1}L^{ij}\left(-\frac12R-2H^2+\frac14G^2\right)\\
&+L^{-3}\left[-N^2L^{ij}-E_0^2L^{ij}
-2E_0^aL^{k(i}\nabla_aL_k{}^{j)}
-L_{kl}\nabla_aL^{k(i}\nabla^aL^{j)l}\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{C8}
```

This is Gold (12b)'s triplet, not a newly named field in the construction. The coefficient in (C7) follows from

```math
6f_0+\frac83T_0^2+4D_0
=-\frac12R-2H^2+\frac14G^2+gN+\frac14g^2L^2.
\tag{C9}
```

Expanding the shifted square gives

```math
[Y']_0^2-2g\frac NL[Y'^{ij}]_0L_{ij}
=\mathbf Y^2+\frac{g^2L}{2}\mathbf Y^{ij}L_{ij}-g^2N^2+\frac1{16}g^4L^4.
\tag{C10}
```

The exact $`SU(2)`$ contraction identities are

```math
\begin{aligned}
L_{ij}L^{k(i}\nabla_aL_k{}^{j)}&=0,\\
L_{ij}L_{kl}\nabla_aL^{k(i}\nabla^aL^{j)l}
&=L^2(\partial L)^2-\frac12L^2\nabla_aL^{ij}\nabla^aL_{ij}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C11}
```

Inserting (C8) and (C11) and keeping the derivative term explicit,

```math
\begin{aligned}
\frac L2\mathbf Y^{ij}L_{ij}
={}&\frac12L^{ij}\nabla^2L_{ij}-\frac14RL^2-H^2L^2+\frac18G^2L^2
-\frac12N^2-\frac12E_0^2-\frac12(\partial L)^2
+\frac14\nabla_aL^{ij}\nabla^aL_{ij}\\
\doteq{}&\frac14L^{ij}\nabla^2L_{ij}-\frac14RL^2-H^2L^2+\frac18G^2L^2
-\frac12N^2-\frac12E_0^2-\frac12(\partial L)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C12}
```

The boundary in the second line is $`\nabla_a(L^{ij}\nabla^aL_{ij})/4`$. Combining (C6), (C10), and (C12) yields the bosonic density

```math
\begin{aligned}
e^{-1}\mathcal L_{[0]}\doteq{}&\mathbf Y^2-2\partial_a(N/L)\partial^a(N/L)
-\frac18\varepsilon_{abcde}C^a[F'^{bc}]_0[F'^{de}]_0\\
&+\frac NL G^{ab}[F'_{ab}]_0-\frac{N^2}{L^2}G^2+4\frac{N^2}{L^2}HG
-\frac14[F'_{ab}]_0[F'^{ab}]_0-4\frac NL H^{ab}[F'_{ab}]_0\\
&+g^2\left(\frac14L^{ij}\nabla^2L_{ij}-\frac14RL^2-H^2L^2+\frac18G^2L^2
-\frac52N^2-\frac12E_0^2-\frac12(\partial L)^2\right)\\
&-4g\frac{N^3}{L^2}+\frac1{16}g^4L^4.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C13}
```

This agrees coefficient by coefficient with Gold (12a), with the field-strength comparison caveat below. The coefficient of $`\mathbf Y^2`$ is one; no overall normalization has been fitted or changed.

### 5.3 Retain the independently checked orientation sign

The bosonic parent map in the project convention is

```math
[F'_{ab}]_0=4\nabla_{[a}(L^{-1}E_{0b]})+2L^{-1}L_{ij}R_{ab}^{ij}(V)
-2L^{-3}L_k{}^l\nabla_{[a}L^{kp}\nabla_{b]}L_{lp}.
\tag{C14}
```

Its coefficient follows from $`\mathcal F_{11}=L^{-1}`$, $`\partial\mathcal F_{11}/\partial L_{ij}=-L^{-3}L^{ij}`$ in Özkan (3.14), and is printed explicitly in (4.12). The identity

```math
L_k{}^l\nabla_{[a}L^{kp}\nabla_{b]}L_{lp}
=-L_{ij}\nabla_{[a}L^{ik}\nabla_{b]}L_k{}^j
\tag{C15}
```

means that the last term has a **plus** sign when expressed in Gold's contracted-index arrangement. The literal printed minus in Gold (12b) is not substituted here.

For an independent test take $`L=1`$, $`L^{ij}=\delta^{ij}/\sqrt2`$ and arbitrary symmetric connection matrices

```math
V_a=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\q&r\end{pmatrix},\qquad
V_b=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&w\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{C16}
```

Direct matrix multiplication gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
\left.2L_{ij}R_{ab}^{ij}(V)\right|_{V^2}&=2\sqrt2(pv-qu+qw-rv),\\
\left.L_k{}^l\nabla_{[a}L^{kp}\nabla_{b]}L_{lp}\right|_{V^2}&=\sqrt2(pv-qu+qw-rv),\\
\left.[F'_{ab}]_0\right|_{V^2}&=2\sqrt2(pv-qu+qw-rv)-2\sqrt2(pv-qu+qw-rv)=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C17}
```

The opposite sign gives $`4\sqrt2(pv-qu+qw-rv)`$. This would contradict the ordinary curl of (20), which has no quadratic connection term. This is a nonzero negative control, not a test made trivial by vanishing connections.

### 5.4 Indices, parity, derivative order, and weights

Every background coefficient carries the indices of its parent: $`T_{ab}`$ antisymmetric, $`Y'_{ij}`$ symmetric, $`\rho'`$ and $`D`$ scalar, $`\lambda'_i`$ a spinor doublet. The products in Section 4.6 contract these same indices in the unchanged source order. The differential-form potential is ordinary; hatted strengths and their derivatives use (23), (30). No independent $`T,\chi,D,f,\phi`$ is left unspecified.

The action rows have even Grassmann parity. Equations (14)–(15) preserve all scalar factors of $`i`$ and transpose every ordered gamma string. No Fierz rearrangement or commuting-spinor assumption is used to collect the action. Full reality of the complete invariant under a Dirac-conjugation convention is not inferred from the ordered coefficient check; the operational source-bar convention is maintained.

Before fixing $`\sigma`$, the source weights are

```math
\begin{gathered}
w(L_{ij})=3,\quad w(N)=w(E_a)=4,\quad w(\varphi)=\frac72,\quad w(\psi_a)=\frac12,\quad
w(\rho')=1,\quad w(\lambda')=\frac32,\quad w(Y')=w(\widehat F')=2,\\
w(T)=1,\quad w(\chi)=\frac32,\quad w(D)=w(f_a{}^a)=2,\quad w(\phi_a)=\frac32.
\end{gathered}
\tag{C18}
```

Representative insertions satisfy

```math
\begin{aligned}
w(L^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j)&=-9+3+7=1=w(\rho'),\\
w(L^{-1}\not{\mathcal D}\varphi)&=-3+1+\frac72=\frac32=w(\lambda'),\\
w(L^{-3}L_{ij}E^2)&=-9+3+8=2=w(Y'),\\
w(L^{-3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\gamma_a\varphi^j)&=-9+3+7=1=w(A'_a),\\
w(\bar\psi_a\phi_b)&=\frac12+\frac32=2=w(R),\\
w(\bar\psi_a\psi_b)&=1\ne2=w(R).
\end{aligned}
\tag{C19}
```

The last line is one reason the naked-gravitino curvature term discussed in the background section cannot be included. Gauge-fixed formulas inherit suppressed powers of the compensator; weights must be tested before setting $`\sigma=1`$. For example the source kinetic term has an extra unprimed scalar of weight one, so $`1+3/2+1+3/2=5`$, and $`\sigma Y'^2`$ has $`1+2+2=5`$. A gauge-fixed equation is not rejected merely because those suppressed compensator powers are no longer printed.

### 5.5 Limits and verification scope

In the zero-fermion limit every retained bilinear in (4), (6), (17), (19), (22), (24), (27), and (30) vanishes; Section 5.2 explicitly derives the resulting bosonic action. In the $`g=0`$ limit, the terms $`g\varphi/8`$, $`\mp gL\psi/2`$, $`gN/4`$, and $`g^2L^2/16`$ in the background disappear, and the $`gE_3/2`$ contribution in $`H_3`$ is removed. No inverse power of $`g`$ occurs anywhere, so this is a regular ungauged limit. The remaining source expressions are precisely the ungauged component maps on the same gauge slice.

For the bosonic flat constant test $`G=H=E_0=V=0`$, $`\partial L=\partial N=R=0`$, equations (C8) and (C13) give

```math
\mathbf Y^{ij}=-N^2L^{-3}L^{ij},\qquad
e^{-1}\mathcal L_{[0]}=\frac{N^4}{L^4}-\frac52g^2N^2-4g\frac{N^3}{L^2}+\frac1{16}g^4L^4.
\tag{C20}
```

This is an algebraic test configuration, not a claimed vacuum. Direct substitution into the original bosonic source groups gives the same polynomial.

The [component-check runner](../../../../checks/run_component_checks.py) checks the retained supercovariant insertion and collection; its [guide](../../../../README.md) lists the executed kernels and temporary reports. The ordered projection and source identities used here are displayed above. The [Step-5 potential proof](08_step5_primed_composite_vector_insertion.md) supplies the full aligned curl identity, without replacing it by a polarization of an on-shell vector equation. No proof of the full local supersymmetry variation of the resulting R² density is claimed.

Equivalently, the first two sums are the 15 bosonic and 80 quadratic ordered terms whose full component definitions have been calculated above. This equation is a finite, directly substitutable specification of the action in the original unprimed fields. It is exact in bosons and in $`g`$ at the retained physical fermion degree; it is not an expansion about a background. The bosonic boundary-equivalent form is Eq. (C13).

All derivative completions must be used: particularly $`[E]_2`$, $`[f]_2`$, $`[D]_2`$, $`[Y']_2`$, $`[\widehat F']_2`$, and $`[\mathcal D\widehat F']_2`$. Replacing those entries by zero would turn this into the earlier formal explicit-degree truncation, which is not the result here.

## 7. Convention Dependence and Remaining Uncertainties

- The local aligned potential requires $`L>0`$ and the Gold-(25) triplet gauge. It is not an unrestricted potential on every triplet patch. The unrestricted Step-4/Step-5 parent maps remain unchanged.
- The checked Özkan orientation sign is retained. The literal sign of the corresponding term in Gold (12b), read in the project's NW–SE convention, remains discrepant. Agreement with Eq. (12a)'s coefficients therefore does not certify literal agreement with all of the printed Eq. (12b).
- The dependent Lorentz curvature uses the primary Weyl-paper reconciliation explained above and the inherited $`+8\bar\psi e\gamma\chi`$ convention lock. The change is explicitly source-derived here, not described as a published erratum or silently applied to old derivations.
- The leading omitted physical degree is four. Fermion-degree truncation is formal Grassmann bookkeeping, not a numerical estimate such as a percentage error. Cubic terms in $`\chi`$ or $`\lambda'`$ and quartic terms in $`D`$ or $`Y'`$ cannot affect the retained even degree two, since derivatives do not lower fermion degree.
- This completes the explicitly specified quadratic component construction under these source locks. A full local supersymmetry/reality certification, the all-fermion Step-6 target, auxiliary dynamics, vacuum selection, and spectra remain separate work. None is inferred from the distribution or bosonic checks.

## 8. Final Result: One Combined Action Through Two Fermions

(C13), with its derivation in Section 5.2; the separate ordered expressions in Section 6 also remain available. In particular, $`L_{ij}=\delta_{ij}L/\sqrt2`$ with $`L>0`$ leaves $`L`$ dynamical and retains the full connection in its covariant derivative.

To obtain this endpoint, take each source group's already distributed products in Section 4.6, retain its degree-zero and degree-two rows, and place them consecutively before moving to the next source group. Thus a product such as $`Y'_{ij}Y'^{ij}`$ contributes $`[Y'_{ij}]_0[Y'^{ij}]_0+[Y'_{ij}]_0[Y'^{ij}]_2+[Y'_{ij}]_2[Y'^{ij}]_0`$; the omitted product $`[Y'_{ij}]_2[Y'^{ij}]_2`$ has degree four. This is the same projection already performed term by term above. Only the order of addition changes. The order of spinors and gamma matrices within each product is preserved, so no additional Grassmann sign is generated. No integration by parts or equation of motion is used in this recombination.

The brackets $`[X]_0`$, $`[X]_1`$, and $`[X]_2`$ denote the explicit component coefficients derived in Eqs. (4)–(32) and (B1)–(B31). They introduce no new fields. In particular, hatted strengths and their differentiated coefficients include the two-fermion completions derived there. The printed result uses these finite component definitions to avoid repeating their longer expressions in every occurrence. It is exact in the bosonic fields and in $`g`$ at physical fermion degree zero and two, under the source qualifications in Section 7.

The recombination check reads the actual endpoint below and compares all 95 printed ordered terms with the 15 plus 80 terms in Section 6. Its exact ordered-polynomial difference is zero. The check also confirms that the complete earlier report, including Eq. (C13), is unchanged. This verifies the recombination; the scope of the underlying physics checks remains that stated in Sections 5 and 7.

## 9. Complete Insertion into the Original Fields

Eq. (U2) is an intermediate component representation, whereas the final action in Section 10 has every component expression inserted. In particular, the final action contains no $`[X]_n`$, no primed multiplet fields, and no dependent $`T`$, $`\chi`$, $`D`$, $`f_a{}^a`$, $`\phi_a{}^i`$, $`K_a{}^{bc}`$ or supercovariant derivative awaiting substitution. The separate bosonic result (C13) is retained above.

### 9.1 Target, conventions and permitted operations

<!-- ASSERT_CONVENTION: metric_signature=mostly_plus (-++++); natural_units=hbar=c=1; index_positioning=NW-SE; gauge_slice=Gold7-and-local-Gold25; fermion_order=physical-0-and-2; background=gauged_Coomans -->

The input is the same Step-4 Eq. (47) density, with the component definitions derived in Eqs. (4)–(32) and (B1)–(B31) above. Those equations supply all coefficients required at this order. The new operation is their complete substitution, ordinary product differentiation, distribution of multiplication over addition, and collection of equal contractions. The source qualifications in Section 7 continue to apply.

The assumptions are: (A1) work off shell in five dimensions with the conventions of Section 2; (A2) use $`\sigma=1`$, $`b_\mu=0`$, defining $`\psi^i=0`$, and the permitted local alignment $`L_{ij}=L\delta_{ij}/\sqrt2`$, $`L>0`$; (A3) keep $`L`$ dynamical, the full $`SU(2)`$ connection and the two surviving fermions $`\psi_\mu{}^i,\varphi^i`$; (A4) retain physical fermion degree zero and two, with the first omitted degree four; (A5) use no field equation, auxiliary elimination, field redefinition or additional integration by parts. No expansion in $`g`$ or around a vacuum is made.

The only fields and kinematic quantities in the final density are $`L,N,L_{ij},G_{ab},H_{ab},E_{abc},V_a,R,\psi_a{}^i,\varphi^i`$ and their ordinary covariant derivatives, with gamma matrices and the fixed index tensors. Here $`E_{abc}`$ is the original ordinary three-form, not the constrained vector $`E_a`$. The ordinary $`G,H`$ and $`R=R(\omega(e))`$ have the definitions already given in (4), (B2) and Section 2. These ordinary strengths and the curvature are retained as the kinematic tensor basis; the primed composite field strength is completely removed.

$`L_{ij}`$ denotes the same aligned original triplet, not an extra independent field. Keeping its ordinary covariant derivatives in tensor notation preserves the connection terms explicitly specified in (5)–(6); they are not set to zero by alignment. Likewise $`\nabla`$ on the surviving spinors is the ordinary Levi–Civita and full bosonic $`SU(2)`$ derivative of (5). It contains no hidden fermion correction. Thus this notation does not split any field into a bosonic and a fermionic piece.

### 9.2 Substitution and product rules

For example, the scalar and its square become, with the original fields written directly,

```math
\begin{aligned}
\rho'&=\frac{2N}{L}+\frac{i}{L^3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j,\\
(\rho')^2&=\frac{4N^2}{L^2}
+2\frac{2N}{L}\frac{i}{L^3}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j
-\frac{1}{L^6}L_{ij}L_{kl}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j\bar\varphi^k\varphi^l\\
&=\frac{4N^2}{L^2}+\frac{4iN}{L^4}L_{ij}\bar\varphi^i\varphi^j
+O(\mathrm{fermion}^4).
\end{aligned}
\tag{E1}
```

The second line multiplies the two factors without moving a fermion. The third line drops precisely the displayed four-fermion monomial. The same degree rule is applied after every multiplication, so a cubic piece of an odd composite cannot enter the quadratic action.

Every derivative acts before products are collected. For a coefficient depending on the original scalars, the ordinary even Leibniz rule gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_a\left(L^{-p}N^q X_1\cdots X_m\right)
={}&-pL^{-p-1}N^q(\partial_aL)X_1\cdots X_m
+qL^{-p}N^{q-1}(\partial_aN)X_1\cdots X_m\\
&+L^{-p}N^q\sum_{r=1}^{m}X_1\cdots(\nabla_aX_r)\cdots X_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{E2}
```

This rule has no extra fermionic sign because the derivative is even. No factor is moved through another odd factor. A second derivative applies this same rule to each displayed summand; derivative order is preserved. In the final result every such product derivative has been distributed: derivatives act on single original fields, not on a still-unexpanded composite or product.

The transpose bar is applied before inserting an odd map into a bilinear. As in (14)–(15), it reverses each gamma string and multiplies a rank-$`p`$ antisymmetrized gamma by $`(-1)^{p(p-1)/2}`$; scalar $`i`$ is preserved in the locked operational bar convention. It does not interchange the two Grassmann-odd factors of the bilinear.

### 9.3 Algebra used to simplify the expanded products

For the $`SU(2)`$ contractions, the NW–SE convention gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^{ij}X_j&=X^i,&\varepsilon^{ij}X_i&=-X^j,\\
\varepsilon_{ij}X^i&=X_j,&\varepsilon_{ij}X^j&=-X_i,\\
L_{ij}L^{jk}&=\frac{L^2}{2}\delta_i{}^k,&L_i{}^i&=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{E3}
```

The first two lines follow directly from the raising/lowering definitions and antisymmetry of epsilon. For the last line, take a general symmetric matrix with entries $`p,q,r`$ and explicitly raise both indices:

```math
\begin{aligned}
L_{ij}&=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\q&r\end{pmatrix},\qquad
L^{ij}=\begin{pmatrix}r&-q\\-q&p\end{pmatrix},\qquad L^2=2(pr-q^2),\\
L_{ij}L^{jk}&=\begin{pmatrix}pr-q^2&0\\0&pr-q^2\end{pmatrix}
=\frac{L^2}{2}\delta_i{}^k,\qquad
L_i{}^i=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\q&r\end{pmatrix}_{ij}\varepsilon^{ij}=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{E4}
```

The symbols $`p,q,r`$ in this check are matrix entries only; none is a field in the final action. The norm contraction is used only on undifferentiated triplets. Derivatives are evaluated before that identity is applied, so a derivative of the aligned triplet cannot be discarded.

When collecting identical scalar contractions, transferring a contracted Lorentz index between the two factors uses $`X^aY_a=X_aY^a`$. Transferring a contracted $`SU(2)`$ index uses $`X^iY_i=-X_iY^i`$, obtained by inserting $`X^i=\varepsilon^{ij}X_j`$ and relabeling the two dummy indices; no fermion is interchanged. These signs are included before coefficients are combined. Mixed upper/lower tensor slots are printed in their original slot order, for example $`G^a{}_b`$ rather than replacing it by $`G_b{}^a`$.

Closed gamma contractions are reduced with the same five-dimensional Clifford algebra. Anticommuting the contracted gamma through an antisymmetrized string gives

```math
\begin{aligned}
\gamma^a\gamma_a&=5,\\
\gamma^a\gamma_{a b_2\ldots b_p}&=(5-p+1)\gamma_{b_2\ldots b_p},\\
\gamma_{b_1\ldots b_{p-1}a}\gamma^a&=(5-p+1)\gamma_{b_1\ldots b_{p-1}},\\
\gamma^a\gamma^{b_1\ldots b_p}\gamma_a
&=(-1)^p(5-2p)\gamma^{b_1\ldots b_p},\\
\gamma^{a_1\ldots a_p}\gamma_{a_1\ldots a_p}
&=(-1)^{p(p-1)/2}\frac{5!}{(5-p)!}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{E5}
```

In the second and third lines the contracted index is in the displayed position; moving it to another position contributes its antisymmetry sign. To see the fourth coefficient, commute the left gamma across the $`p`$ antisymmetrized entries. The term that crosses all entries contributes $`(-1)^p5`$ after the final contraction. Each of the $`p`$ anticommutators contributes $`-2(-1)^p`$, giving $`(-1)^p(5-2p)`$. Iterating the second/third-line contraction gives the last line and its reversal sign. These identities are used only when the contracted index occurs inside that gamma string, with no other occurrence elsewhere in the monomial.

Gamma strings whose indices contract with different external tensors remain in their original matrix order. The chosen expression is an ordered gamma-string basis, not a claimed minimal Fierz basis. Identical contractions in this basis are collected after dummy-index relabeling. Ordinary even tensor coefficients may commute; the two fermions never interchange. Tensor antisymmetry is applied to $`G,H,E_{abc}`$, epsilon and antisymmetrized gamma matrices; triplet symmetry is applied to $`L_{ij}`$.

### 9.4 Complete field insertions

The following equalities write the component expressions needed in the action directly in the original fields. They are continued over several displays solely for readability. The odd maps are shown through one fermion, sufficient wherever they occur in the even action; the even maps are shown through two. They have no projected-field notation. All derivative products have been distributed. The unchanged component derivations above fix their source coefficients; (E2)–(E5) explain the subsequent operations.

A useful direct check isolates the curvature square. The curvature part of the substituted triplet is $`-RL_{ij}/(2L)`$, hence

```math
\left(-\frac{R}{2L}L^{ij}\right)\left(-\frac{R}{2L}L_{ij}\right)
=\frac{R^2}{4L^2}L^{ij}L_{ij}
=\frac14R^2.
\tag{E6}
```

The final expansion contains exactly this coefficient. The constant, zero-flux, zero-fermion check of (C20) can also be obtained directly before collection. In that restriction,

```math
\begin{aligned}
Y'_{ij}&=\left(-\frac{N^2}{L^3}+\frac{gN}{L}+\frac{g^2L}{4}\right)L_{ij},\\
Y'^{ij}Y'_{ij}-\frac{2gN}{L}Y'^{ij}L_{ij}
&=\frac{N^4}{L^4}-\frac32g^2N^2+\frac1{16}g^4L^4,\\
e^{-1}\mathcal L_{R^2}\big|_{\rm flat,const.,bos.}
&=\frac{N^4}{L^4}-\frac32g^2N^2+\frac1{16}g^4L^4
-g^2N^2-4g\frac{N^3}{L^2}\\
&=\frac{N^4}{L^4}-\frac52g^2N^2-4g\frac{N^3}{L^2}+\frac1{16}g^4L^4.
\end{aligned}
\tag{E7}
```

This checks coefficients on a test configuration and is not a vacuum assertion. The ungauged limit is regular because the final coefficients contain nonnegative powers of $`g`$ only.

For dimensional analysis on the fixed-compensator slice, use engineering dimensions $`[\nabla]=[g]=[N]=[G]=[H]=[V_a]=1`$, $`[L]=[L_{ij}]=[E_{abc}]=0`$, $`[\psi_a]=[\varphi]=1/2`$, and $`[R]=2`$. Every printed monomial has dimension four. These are the engineering dimensions of the gauge-fixed invariant; they do not replace the pre-gauge Weyl weights in (C18)–(C19). The curvature-squared coupling has dimension minus two relative to the two-derivative density.

The exact re-insertion comparison passes **93/93 scoped checks**: every source group agrees with a separate expansion of the earlier 95-row component ledger, all final indices are contracted with opposite variance, every monomial has dimension four, and no dependent or primed field remains. The independent tensor check passes **180/180 checks**, including five-dimensional Clifford matrices and 140 deterministic Einstein-contraction tests with two formal Grassmann generators. Their largest scaled residual is $`4.83e-16`$.

For the latter check, a fermionic jet is assigned coefficients of two anticommuting generators; an ordered product contributes the coefficient $`x_1y_2-x_2y_1`$. This tests the quadratic Grassmann coefficient rather than replacing the fermions by commuting spinors. The general triplet norm and the closed gamma identities are also checked separately.

After collecting equal contractions and distributing scalar coefficient sums, the final density contains **4902 explicit monomials**. This count reflects the decision to print every repeated field expression rather than use composite abbreviations. The verification outputs are `build/step6_elementary_verification.json` and `build/step6_elementary_tensor_verification.json`; the complete per-group algebra is retained in `build/step6_elementary_ledger.json`.
